_readme: Events that happen during a stage. Each event has a stage, a station (a place on the ship) and facts written as { "value": ..., "source": ... }. A source is a link, a written game-design choice, or the word PLACEHOLDER (made up for now; a student replaces it before the final submission). The Mars shadow pass is NOT here: it is a Mars-orbit event and lives in game_data.json (events, power_low). The words on the screen are in data/inner_voice.json (flight) and data/story.json (flight). The science pass (stage arrival) is also here: windows in seconds, storage and downlink hours. The antenna speed and the camera data come from the parts. FLIGHT (batch 9): the Flight plan and its three events (water leak, air leak, food spoils) are in flight_plan, water_leak, air_leak and food_spoil. drain_per_second = how much of the supply an event pours out every real second.

station.source: Game-design choice: the Water station in the Life Support room (A10).

fix.source: Game-design choice: press E at the Water station.

drain_per_second.source: PLACEHOLDER (liters of water lost every real second until the leak is fixed; a leak fixed within about 30 s of the warning leaves the water out of the red)

capture_start_seconds.source: PLACEHOLDER (seconds after the Arrival walk starts; the shadow pass owns 20 to 40 s, so the windows stay outside it)

downlink_end_seconds.source: PLACEHOLDER (the mission clock ends at 60 s)

capture_days_worth.source: PLACEHOLDER (how many days of the camera's data one picture holds, in Gb per day times this)

storage_gb.source: PLACEHOLDER (a fixed onboard storage size in Gb; a student looks up the real recorder size)

downlink_hours.source: PLACEHOLDER (hours the ground station is in view; a student looks up the real contact time)

result_show_seconds.source: PLACEHOLDER (how long the ring stays on screen after the press)

power_note.value: camera off = no capture, antenna off = nothing sent
power_note.source: Game rule: uses the Reroute Power switches

antenna_speed_note.value: Mb/s come from game_data.json parts > antenna > communications (real NASA numbers, sourced there)

surface_work._readme: The surface work (Stage 4, surface destinations): a walkable area, a surface clock, and one task: collect the sample with a timed press (E). max_days = the most days a surface stay can have. The parts decide the real number of days: days = the smallest of (max_days), (spare power / power_cost_per_day_w) and (how many days the crew supplies from Flight last, when each surface day uses supply_days_per_day days of food, water and air). seconds_per_day = real seconds for one surface day. Every day costs power_cost_per_day_w of spare power. Every try (Perfect, Good or Miss) costs attempt_power_cost_w (the drill). A Miss also loses miss_days_lost day (the lander is moved). The sample is sample_distance_m meters from the lander, plus the 'distance' percent from a bad landing. A broken solar panel (landing damage) makes solar power smaller by that percent. Success rules are in game_data.json arrival_goals.

seconds_per_day.source: PLACEHOLDER (real seconds for one surface day)

power_cost_per_day_w.source: PLACEHOLDER (watts of spare power each surface day uses up)

attempt_power_cost_w.source: PLACEHOLDER (watts of spare power one sample try uses)

supply_days_per_day.source: PLACEHOLDER (one surface day uses this many days of the crew's food, water and air)

miss_days_lost.source: PLACEHOLDER (days lost after a missed sample try)

sample_distance_m.source: PLACEHOLDER (meters from the lander to the sample)

result_show_seconds.source: PLACEHOLDER (how long the ring stays on screen after the press)

end_read_seconds.source: PLACEHOLDER (seconds to read the last line before the report)

flyby_pass._readme: The Europa flyby (Stage 4, flyby destinations): four timed presses with SPACE from mission control, then the pass. point_instrument and capture decide how much data is captured: captured = camera Gb per day x capture_days_worth x the point factor x the capture factor (never more than storage_gb). protect_computer decides the radiation loss: loss percent = radiation_loss_percent x (1 - the radiation shield's protection) x the press's loss factor. send_data sends min(what is stored, the antenna's real speed x downlink_hours x the press factor). planned_gb = the least data that must get home for MISSION SUCCESS. The radio delay is the real one from destinations.json.

planned_gb.source: PLACEHOLDER (a student sets a goal from a real mission)

capture_days_worth.source: PLACEHOLDER (days of the camera's data one flyby captures, in Gb per day times this)

storage_gb.source: PLACEHOLDER (same onboard storage size as the Mars science pass)

downlink_hours.source: PLACEHOLDER (hours the ground station listens to the data)

radiation_loss_percent.source: PLACEHOLDER (percent of the stored data a bad radiation hit destroys, with no shield). NASA: near Jupiter the Galileo orbiter faced '25 times more radiation than the level considered deadly for humans': https://science.nasa.gov/mission/galileo/

pass_seconds.source: PLACEHOLDER (real seconds the pass animation takes)

flight_plan._readme: The Flight plan (Stage 3). legs = the legs of the trip in order. Each leg has tasks (ids from the tasks list below; a task the ship cannot do, such as harvest without a garden, is left out) and one event (an id from this file: water_leak, air_leak or food_spoil). Every leg stands for trip_days divided by the number of legs (destinations.json) and lasts flight_leg_seconds. A trip with no crew plays no_crew_legs leg(s) and has no tasks or events. Each task has a station on the ship, the crew supply it looks after, and skip_loss_percent = how much of that meter's full size is lost at the end of the leg if the task was skipped (a skipped task makes its meter drop faster). A leak or spoil that is not fixed stops when the leg ends. Rationing is on for the rest of the trip once it is on.

no_crew_legs.source: Game-design choice (agent's choice for Kaleb, 2026-11-13): a trip with no crew has no crew supplies, so it has no tasks to play; it keeps one leg, as before.

legs.source: GAME_PLAN.md section 6b: 3 legs, each with 2-3 routine tasks and 1 event. Which task and event go in which leg is a game-design choice (agent's choice for Kaleb, 2026-11-13).

skip_loss_percent.source: Game-design choice: skipping the ration has no extra loss, because the crew simply eats the normal amount.

needs_part.source: Game rule: only a ship with a garden (life support part) can harvest.
